non_obvious_official_guidance: Norway Immigration Act distinguishes EEA nationals (right of residence, registration-only path) from non-EEA/third-country nationals (work permit required before entry).
non_obvious_actual_reality: Norway is EEA but NOT EU. HR generalists from EU countries routinely apply intra-EU rules to Norway and trigger the wrong document checklist — wrong form set, wrong authority, wrong timeline. Switzerland and Liechtenstein have separate bilateral agreements that compound the confusion. An EU employee moving to Norway is an EEA move with distinct rights and forms.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm passport nationality. Cross-reference against EEA country list (EU + Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway + Switzerland bilateral) — not the EU list. Set employee_type in case BEFORE any applications are filed or any UDI portal is touched.

deadline_label: At least 3 weeks before move date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers may apply for a D-number on behalf of new employees using form RF-1401 or via Altinn. The D-number is a temporary national identification number valid until a permanent personnummer is issued.
non_obvious_actual_reality: D-number takes 2–4 weeks to arrive. Without it: no bank account, no skattekort, no NAV registration, no correct payroll deduction. Employers who don't initiate this before the employee's move date create a cascade of blocked first-month steps. Many HR teams don't know they can (and should) initiate — they wait for the employee to request it after arrival, which means a 4–6 week delay into the employee's first month.
non_obvious_action_required: HR initiates D-number application the day the signed contract is received — not after the employee arrives. Track the Altinn submission reference. Confirm estimated processing time with Skatteetaten at submission.

deadline_label: Within 3 months of arrival for stays longer than 3 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: EEA nationals exercising right of residence in Norway for more than 3 months must register with the police. This is a registration — not a permit application — but it is legally required.
non_obvious_actual_reality: This step is invisible to most HR teams because it's framed as the employee's individual responsibility — but HR is equally exposed to a compliance failure if it's missed. Police appointment slots in Oslo have wait times of 3–6 weeks. If HR doesn't book this before the employee's move date, the deadline slips into week seven, exactly when compliance problems surface.
non_obvious_action_required: HR pre-books the police registration appointment via politiet.no BEFORE the employee's move date. Employee attends in person with: original passport, signed employment contract, and proof of accommodation address. Bring originals — copies are rejected.

non_obvious_official_guidance: To open a Norwegian bank account you typically need a Norwegian ID number (D-number or personnummer) and proof of Norwegian address.
non_obvious_actual_reality: D-number required → bank account. Bank account required → salary payment. D-number takes 2–4 weeks. If HR doesn't apply for the D-number before the employee arrives, the employee cannot open a bank account on arrival, which means the first paycheck has no destination. Some banks (DNB) have an employer-coordination path that can open an account before D-number arrives — but it requires HR to initiate it and it is not publicised.
non_obvious_action_required: Apply for D-number at least 3 weeks before move date. Employee opens bank account on first working day using D-number. HR confirms bank account number is received before payroll close date for first month.

deadline_label: Before first paycheck — employer legally required to deduct 50% tax without it
non_obvious_official_guidance: All employees working in Norway must have a skattekort. Employers retrieve it digitally from Skatteetaten using the employee's D-number or personnummer.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Without skattekort, the employer is legally required to deduct 50% tax — the emergency rate. This triggers employee panic about their first paycheck. HR teams who don't proactively obtain skattekort before payroll close discover the problem retroactively. The skattekort cannot be applied for without a D-number — creating a dependent chain: D-number → skattekort → correct payroll deduction.
non_obvious_action_required: As soon as D-number is received, employee applies for skattekort at skatteetaten.no. HR confirms employer has digitally retrieved it from Skatteetaten before the payroll close date for the first salary payment. Do not wait — the portal retrieval is instantaneous once issued.

source: NAV.no — membership in National Insurance Scheme

field_label: Residence permit granted date and permit number
deadline_label: Must be granted before employment start — no right to work without it

field_label: National Identity Number (personnummer) — replaces D-number after 6 months residence
deadline_label: Issued automatically after 6 months of registered residence — update all registrations immediately
non_obvious_official_guidance: After 6 months of lawful and registered residence in Norway, foreign nationals are assigned a permanent National Identity Number (personnummer) to replace their temporary D-number.
non_obvious_actual_reality: D-number and personnummer are NOT interchangeable. An employee who has been on a D-number for 6 months will find the D-number stops working for key services — BankID, Altinn — when the personnummer is issued. If HR is not tracking this, the employee gets locked out of digital services without warning and has to chase updates to bank, payroll, NAV, and Skatteetaten individually. HR is rarely notified; the employee receives a letter.
non_obvious_action_required: HR tracks the 6-month anniversary from move date. At that point, employee checks Folkeregisteret for personnummer issuance. On receipt: update Skatteetaten (skattekort), NAV membership record, bank (for BankID), and employer payroll system — in that order.
source: Folkeregisterloven; Skatteetaten — National Identity Number guidance
